title: Creating your first wiki
description: Create a hosting account and your first wiki.

sections.heading: Your hosting account
sections.html: Register at the hosting portal. Follow any email verification or account approval steps shown there. If approval is required, wait for the decision before creating a wiki.

sections.heading: Create the wiki
sections.html: Choose New wiki on Your wikis and complete the form. The portal shows the address, the initial administrator credentials, the service expiry and the storage limit. Save the credentials and open the wiki to begin. Wiki accounts and hosting accounts are separate. What your wiki includes lists everything it can do.

title: What your wiki includes
description: Everything a new wiki can do, and what is switched on from the start.

sections.heading: Pages and editing
sections.html:
Pages are written in Markdown, with a live preview beside the editor. You can import a .md or .txt file into a page, attach files and images, embed videos, and export any page as Markdown or PDF or print it. Drafts are saved while you type, so closing the tab does not lose your work.

Pages live in categories, which can be nested, and the sidebar search finds pages and categories by name. Administrators can import or export many pages at once with Bulk Markdown. The Page builder lays out a page without writing Markdown; on this service it has to be allowed for your wiki first.

sections.heading: History and review
sections.html:
Every save is kept. A page's history shows what changed between two revisions and lets you restore an earlier one.

With Page governance an editor can reserve a page while working on it, or protect it so only they can edit it; an administrator can remove a protection 72 hours after asking. With Contribution approval, changes proposed by people without edit rights wait for a reviewer. The Deletion slowdown plugin holds a deleted page for 48 hours so an administrator can bring it back.

sections.heading: People and access
sections.html:
Every account has a role: user, editor, administrator or owner. Administrators can also build custom roles from individual permissions, and limit reading and editing to particular categories. New members join with an invite code or by signing up, and sign-ups can require approval.

A wiki is private by default. Public read access is optional and, on this service, has to be allowed for your wiki. The Temporary accounts and pages plugin removes accounts, pages or elevated roles on a date you choose.

sections.heading: Working together
sections.html:
• Kanban boards with tickets, comments, attachments and a history of changes.
  • Canvas diagrams that mix text, images and video with links to wiki pages.
  • Chats and groups for direct messages and group conversations inside the wiki.
  • Announcements for banners shown across the site.
  • User profiles with a bio, an avatar and a map of each person's contributions.

sections.heading: Reading and learning
sections.html:
• Read aloud reads pages in English and Italian (German once an administrator turns it on), using Piper voices on the server.
  • Assessments add polls and quizzes to a page, with points and limits on attempts.
  • Badges are awarded by hand or automatically, for example after a number of contributions.
  • Difficulty tags label pages by level.

sections.heading: Administration
sections.html:
The interface is available in English, Italian and German, and administrators can add another language. Easy mode (BM mode), which you can tick when you create the wiki, starts it in BM mode, the wiki's easy mode: fewer features and simpler screens for groups that mostly need pages. The wiki's administrators adjust it under Administration → BM mode, and each member can choose the simple or the full interface for themselves. Members can start a guided tour from their settings, and administrators can show it to everyone who joins.

The REST API gives scripts access through tokens limited to chosen areas. The Custom pages plugin publishes content at an address you pick. Every member can download their own data from their settings, and Site migration exports the whole wiki as one archive.

sections.heading: Switched on from the start
sections.html: A new wiki starts with Announcements, Assessments, Attachments, Audit log, Badges, Canvas, Chats and groups, Difficulty tags, Drafts, Kanban boards, Mascot, Page history, Personal data export, Read aloud and User profiles enabled. The Recommended setup, offered when the wiki opens for the first time, keeps exactly these. In Easy mode (BM mode), Assessments, Chats and groups and Read aloud start hidden, and Canvas and Kanban boards start in a simpler form; administrators can show any of them under Administration → BM mode. The other plugins are one click away; see Managing plugins.

title: Running your wiki
description: Members, settings and pages inside the wiki.

sections.heading: Members and roles
sections.html: In the wiki, open Administration. Users creates accounts and changes roles, Invite codes makes codes for the sign-up page, and Site settings decides whether people can sign up themselves and whether sign-ups wait for approval. The roles are user, editor, administrator and owner; Custom roles and category access narrow them further. Wiki accounts are separate from accounts on this portal.

sections.heading: Settings and privacy
sections.html: Site settings also holds the wiki's name and time zone, and Appearance its colours. A wiki is private: only signed-in members can read it. Public read access has to be allowed for your wiki on this service before it can be switched on. The operators of this service can reach the data on the server for operation and support; see the privacy policy.

sections.heading: Pages and files
sections.html: Click New page in the sidebar to write a page in Markdown. Images and attachments count towards the wiki's storage limit, which the portal shows on the wiki's page. For a full user guide inside the wiki, open Administration, then Documentation, which adds one as a category of pages.

title: Managing plugins
description: Turn the optional parts of your wiki on and off.

sections.heading: Where to find them
sections.html: In the wiki, open the account menu, choose Administration, then Plugins under Wiki settings. Disabling a plugin hides its pages and menus. Its content and settings stay, and come back when you enable it again.

sections.heading: The built-in plugins
sections.html:
These ship with every wiki, under the names the Plugins page shows. The ones marked on are enabled when a wiki is created.

  • Announcements (on): banners shown across the site.
  • Assessments (on): polls and quizzes on a page, with points and attempt limits.
  • Attachments (on): files attached to pages.
  • Audit log (on): a record of sign-ins, account and role changes, deletions and settings changes.
  • Badges (on): awards given by hand or automatically.
  • Canvas (on): diagrams with text, images, video and links to pages.
  • Chats and groups (on): direct messages and group conversations.
  • Custom pages: content published at an address you choose.
  • Deletion slowdown: deleted pages are held for 48 hours before they go.
  • Difficulty tags (on): labels for the level of a page.
  • Drafts (on): drafts saved while you edit.
  • Kanban boards (on): boards, tickets, comments and attachments.
  • Mascot (on): a pixel-art banana in the top bar.
  • Page governance: page reservations and protection.
  • Page history (on): revisions, differences and restoring an earlier version.
  • Personal data export (on): each member can download their own data.
  • Read aloud (on): pages read aloud by voices running on the server.
  • REST API: personal tokens, each limited to chosen areas, with a log of their use.
  • Temporary accounts and pages: accounts, pages and roles that expire on a schedule.
  • User profiles (on): profile pages with a bio, an avatar and a contribution map.

sections.heading: Plugins from elsewhere
sections.html: If the operator of this service allows them, the Plugins page can also import a .bwplugin file written by someone else. A plugin is Python code and runs with the wiki's own access to its data and network, so install only code you trust. On this service each wiki runs in its own container, and the operator can switch off every third-party plugin on a wiki at once if one causes trouble.

title: Exports and backups
description: Export your wiki and what the platform backs up.

sections.heading: Export your wiki
sections.html: In the wiki, open Administration, then Site migration under System, and in Export the whole site choose Export for a complete archive of the wiki: content, accounts, files and settings. Only the wiki's owners and superusers can do this. It is the copy to keep, and the one to use if you move the wiki to your own server. For pages only, Bulk Markdown exports them as Markdown files, and any single page can be exported as Markdown or PDF from its own menu. Members can download their personal data from their settings.

sections.heading: Platform backups
sections.html: Platform backups are managed by the service operator. Contact support to check which restore points and retention periods are available for your wiki. Keep your own exports; a service backup is not a substitute for a copy you control.

title: Moving your wiki to your own server
description: Take a complete copy of your wiki and run it yourself.

sections.heading: Before you start
sections.html: BananaWiki is free software under the GNU AGPL, and the source this service runs is published in the BananaWiki source repository. A wiki moves across with its pages, accounts, history and files. You need the wiki's owner account (the one created with the wiki) and somewhere to run the new one: a Linux server, or for a small group the desktop launcher, built from the source, on Windows, Linux or a Mac with Apple silicon.

sections.heading: 1. Export the wiki
sections.html:
In the wiki you are moving, open Administration, then Site migration under System, and in Export the whole site choose Export. The ZIP holds every table (accounts, pages, categories, settings, chats, boards and more), uploaded images and attachments, custom icons and the site configuration.

Keep the file private: it contains everything in the wiki, including account records.

sections.heading: 2. Install BananaWiki
sections.html:
Pick the route that fits:

  • A Linux server. From a checkout of the source, sudo ./banana install --mode wiki installs the service, and the deployment guide covers HTTPS, backups and updates.
  • Linux or macOS with Python 3.11 or newer. Follow the quick start in the README.
  • A desktop computer. The launcher is built from the source; see the desktop launcher guide.

Open the new wiki and finish the setup page with a temporary administrator account.

sections.heading: 3. Import the export
sections.html:
Signed in as that administrator, open Administration, then Site migration. Under Replace this site with an export, select the export file, tick I understand that this replaces all data on this wiki, enter Your password and choose Import and replace.

The temporary administrator is replaced by the accounts from the export, so sign in again with your usual username and password. Everyone else keeps theirs, except members who only ever signed in through the hosting portal: they have no password of their own, so an administrator sets one for them on the new server.

sections.heading: After the move
sections.html:
• Point your domain at the new server. Members sign in again, because sessions from the old one do not carry over.
  • Settings stored encrypted with the old server's key, such as a remote read-aloud token, read as empty and need to be entered again.
  • Automatic updates are off until you turn them on, and backups are yours to set up; the deployment guide explains both.
  • If anything is missing, the original export is still your complete copy.

title: Managing your account and wikis
description: Review account access and look after your wikis.

sections.heading: Account security
sections.html: Use the Account page to update your profile and password, manage two-step verification and review the signed-in devices. Save your recovery codes privately. Sign out the devices you no longer recognise.

sections.heading: Wiki actions
sections.html:
On a wiki's page, under Wiki controls, Stop takes the wiki offline and keeps its files; a stopped wiki shows a Start button at the top of its page and in the list of your wikis, which brings the same wiki back. Terminate, under Reset or terminate wiki, takes the wiki offline and keeps its data for the retention period shown in the portal; deleting it permanently, or the end of that period, removes the data for good.

Reset admin password gives the wiki's administrator a new temporary password, signs that account out everywhere and turns off its two-step verification: use it when you are locked out of your wiki, even after losing your authenticator app and recovery codes. Once you are back in, turn two-step verification on again in the wiki's settings.

title: Protecting your wiki
description: Use strong account controls and choose who can do what.

sections.heading: Accounts and content
sections.html: Use a unique password and turn on two-step verification for your hosting account. On a wiki's page, remove collaborators who no longer need access. Install only plugins you trust; see Managing plugins.

sections.heading: Report a problem
sections.html: Report suspected account compromise or service abuse to {contact_email}. For a vulnerability in the software, follow the private reporting instructions in the BananaWiki project's security policy. Do not post credentials or private wiki content in public issues.

title: Common issues and fixes
description: Find the next step when a wiki is unavailable.

sections.heading: A wiki does not open
sections.html: Check the wiki's status and expiry on Your wikis. A stopped wiki starts again with Start; if your account is suspended or was not approved, sort that out with the platform administrators first. Use the address the service assigned while diagnosing a custom-domain problem.

sections.heading: Ask for help
sections.html: Include the wiki address, approximate time, action attempted, and visible error. Describe whether the problem affects every user or one account. Never send passwords, recovery codes, backup keys or authenticator codes.

title: Email verification
description: Add and verify a contact address when requested.

sections.heading: Verification steps
sections.html: If the portal asks for email verification, use the link sent to your contact address. Check spam folders and the address entered on the Account page. The portal shows when another verification email can be requested.

sections.heading: An address is no longer available
sections.html: Update the address on the Account page using your current password. If you cannot sign in, contact support for account recovery. Verification does not itself approve a pending account.

title: Wiki expiry and renewal
description: When a wiki expires, how to renew it and how long data is kept.

sections.heading: Service expiry
sections.html: Your wikis shows how long each wiki has left. In the last days before a wiki expires, its page offers Renew, which gives it the number of days shown on the button, counted from the day you renew. The owner, or a collaborator allowed to start and stop the wiki, can renew it. If the button is not offered, ask support for an extension. These hosting limits are separate from the AGPL software licence, which permits personal and commercial self-hosting.

sections.heading: Recovery
sections.html: After termination, retained data may be restored during the retention period shown in the portal, and the wiki's page may offer a download until then. Contact support promptly and quote the wiki address. Recovery cannot be promised after the retained files have been deleted. Export important content before expiry.

title: Using a custom domain
description: Connect a domain you control to an approved wiki.

sections.heading: Permission and DNS
sections.html: Open Custom domain on the wiki's page. If your wiki may not use one yet, ask for it there: the platform's administrators answer on that page and by email. Once it is allowed, add the domain: a subdomain such as docs.example.org (one CNAME record) or your root domain such as example.org (A/AAAA records). The page shows each record the way DNS providers ask for it (type, name, value) with Copy buttons, and tips for Cloudflare and other providers. Keep those records in place.

sections.heading: Verification and HTTPS
sections.html: While the page is open it checks your records every half minute, shows which are found, missing or wrong, and turns the domain on as soon as both are right; Check DNS now checks at once. A hostname that is not verified within an hour expires: add it again and replace the TXT value with the new one the portal shows. HTTPS becomes available within a minute of verification. If permission is revoked, verification lapses, or the wiki is suspended, the custom domain stops routing. The technical DNS guide explains the checks.

title: Using the hosting API
description: Create a token so a script can read your wikis and stop or start them.

sections.heading: Before you start
sections.html: The hosting API lets a script or another program read your account and your wikis, and stop (pause) or start (resume) a wiki, without signing in to the portal. The operator of this service has to switch it on first. If your Account page has no API tokens section, the API is not available to your account.

sections.heading: Creating a token
sections.html: Open Account and go to API tokens. Give the token a name that reminds you where it is used, tick the Permissions it needs, choose when it expires and confirm with your current password. The token is shown once, straight after you create it, so copy it then. If you lose it, revoke it and create another.

sections.heading: What a token can do
sections.html:
• account:read reads your username and contact email.
  • instances:read lists your wikis, and the wikis shared with you, with their status and storage.
  • instances:manage stops (pause) and starts (resume) a wiki.
  • admin:read, offered only to platform administrators, reads the approval queue and wiki totals.

On a wiki someone shared with you, a token can do only what your collaborator permissions allow. The API cannot delete, reset or download a wiki; the portal still does those.

sections.heading: Using and protecting it
sections.html: Send the token in the Authorization header of each request, as Bearer followed by the token, to /api/v1 on this portal. For example, /api/v1/instances lists your wikis. Keep a token as private as a password and revoke the ones you no longer use. Changing or resetting your password revokes all of them. Switching the API off does not: your tokens stop working while it is off and work again when it is back on, so revoke the ones you no longer want. BananaWiki's API reference lists every request.

title: Contact and support
description: Contact the hosted service or contribute to the software.

sections.heading: Hosted service
sections.html: Email {contact_email} for account recovery, hosting extensions, domain permissions, or abuse reports. Include your portal username and wiki address when relevant, without passwords or keys.

sections.heading: Source and contributions
sections.html: The source this service runs is published in the BananaWiki source repository under the AGPL, version 3. Use public issues for reproducible software bugs and feature requests, with private data removed. Read the BananaWiki project's contribution guide before opening a pull request.
